mergedParams.userDescription: Minimalist text with a slow, continuous, almost imperceptible zoom. typo kinetics for titles/captions/other text..

output.title: Minimalist Typokinetic Text with Subtle Continuous Zoom

prompts.prompt: Create a minimalist typographic preset with an almost subliminal continuous zoom effect. Think of it like a dolly zoom in cinematography - the text should appear static at first glance, but over the course of 5-10 seconds, it should scale from 100% to 102-103% with a perfectly linear easing. The text should be centered both horizontally and vertically, using a clean sans-serif font. The zoom should originate from the exact center of the text, creating a hypnotic, meditative quality. Consider this as a title card that holds attention through subtle motion rather than dramatic animation. The effect should be so slow that viewers might not consciously notice it, but they'll feel its presence - like the barely perceptible zoom on a Ken Burns photo effect.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Use a single BaseLayout container with 'flex items-center justify-center w-full h-full' for perfect centering. Inside, place a TextAtom with the caption data. Apply a generic keyframe effect with scale transformation from 1.0 to 1.03 over the full duration using linear easing. Set transform-origin to center. Use 'font-sans text-4xl md:text-6xl font-light tracking-wide text-gray-900' for typography. Add 'will-change-transform' to the container style for GPU acceleration. Set the effect range to [{at: 0, value: 1}, {at: 1, value: 1.03}] with easing: 'linear'. Consider using fitDurationTo: 'children' to match the caption duration. The slow zoom creates a Ken Burns-like effect that's almost imperceptible but adds visual interest.

prompts.prompt: Design a word-by-word reveal preset where each word arrives with its own micro-zoom animation. Picture this as if you're using a zoom lens to focus on each word as it appears - starting at 95% scale with 0 opacity, then animating to 100% scale with full opacity over 200ms. The zoom should have a slight overshoot (to 101%) before settling at 100%, like a camera autofocus finding its mark. Words should cascade with a 50-100ms stagger between them. After all words are revealed, apply the continuous slow zoom to the entire text block, scaling from 100% to 102% over the remaining duration. This creates a two-phase animation: dynamic word reveals followed by the meditative continuous zoom.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Create a BaseLayout with 'flex flex-wrap items-center justify-center gap-2 w-full h-full px-8'. Map through caption.words array to create individual TextAtom components for each word. For each word, use its relative timing (word.relativeStart) to trigger a scale effect from 0.95 to 1.01 to 1.0 with opacity from 0 to 1. Use 'ease-out' for the initial zoom, then 'ease-in-out' for the settle. Apply 'inline-block transform-gpu' to each word container. After the last word's animation (calculate from words array), apply a parent-level scale effect from 1.0 to 1.02 over the remaining duration. Use internal effect presets for the word reveals if available, or create custom effects with AnimationRange. Consider creating a sub-preset for the word reveal logic to keep the main preset clean.

prompts.prompt: Build a perspective-based zoom preset that simulates a camera slowly tracking forward through 3D space. Instead of a flat scale, use CSS perspective and translateZ to create genuine depth. The text should feel like it's floating in space, slowly moving toward the viewer. Start with perspective(1000px) translateZ(-50px) and animate to translateZ(10px) over the full duration. This creates a more cinematic, three-dimensional zoom that's subtle but has more visual interest than a simple scale. Add a very slight rotation on the Y-axis (0 to 2 degrees) to enhance the 3D effect, as if the camera is slightly panning while zooming.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Use BaseLayout with 'relative w-full h-full overflow-hidden' and style={{ perspective: '1000px' }}. Inside, create another BaseLayout with 'absolute inset-0 flex items-center justify-center preserve-3d' (add style={{ transformStyle: 'preserve-3d' }}). Apply a TextAtom with combined transform effects: translateZ from -50 to 10, rotateY from 0 to 2. Use 'text-6xl font-thin tracking-widest uppercase' for a cinematic title feel. Create two parallel effects in the effects array - one for translateZ with easing: 'ease-in-out', another for rotateY with easing: 'linear'. The perspective creates genuine depth rather than flat scaling. Consider adding a subtle text-shadow for depth: 'shadow-2xl' or custom textShadow in effects.

prompts.prompt: Create a breathing zoom preset where the text pulsates gently like a living organism. Instead of a linear zoom, use a sine wave pattern that scales between 99% and 101% in a continuous loop. Each 'breath' cycle should last 3-4 seconds. Layer this with an overall growth from 100% to 102% over the full duration. This creates an organic, meditative quality - like watching someone breathe while slowly zooming in with a camera. The breathing should be subtle enough to feel natural, not mechanical. Think of this as combining a slow dolly zoom with the natural camera shake from a handheld shot, but using scale instead of position.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Use BaseLayout with 'flex items-center justify-center w-full h-full'. Create a custom effect function in presetExecution that generates a sine wave scale pattern. Calculate the number of breath cycles based on duration (duration / 3.5 seconds per cycle). Generate an AnimationRange array with multiple keyframes following Math.sin() values mapped between 0.99 and 1.01. Overlay a second scale effect that goes from 1.0 to 1.02 linearly. Combine both transforms using separate effects or merge the values. Use 'transform-gpu will-change-transform' for smooth animation. Typography: 'text-5xl font-normal text-gray-800'. Consider using a spring easing for more organic motion, or create a custom cubic-bezier for the breathing pattern.

prompts.prompt: Design a parallax zoom preset where different text elements zoom at slightly different rates, creating depth through motion parallax. Split the text into three layers: background (slowest zoom 100% to 101%), main text (medium zoom 100% to 102%), and emphasis words (fastest zoom 100% to 103%). This mimics how objects at different distances move at different speeds when a camera zooms. Keywords or impactful words should be in the foreground layer. Use opacity and blur to enhance the depth illusion - background text slightly blurred and 70% opacity, foreground text sharp and full opacity.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Create nested BaseLayout containers with 'absolute inset-0' positioning. Use caption metadata to identify keywords (caption.words.filter(w => w.metadata?.keyword)). Create three layers: background BaseLayout with 'opacity-70' and filter: 'blur(0.5px)', middle layer normal, foreground with 'font-semibold'. Apply different scale effects to each layer - background: [{at: 0, value: 1}, {at: 1, value: 1.01}], main: [{at: 0, value: 1}, {at: 1, value: 1.02}], foreground: [{at: 0, value: 1}, {at: 1, value: 1.03}]. Use z-index or natural stacking. Consider using containerProps.className for each layer. This creates a multi-plane camera effect similar to traditional animation techniques.

prompts.prompt: Build a focus-pull zoom preset that simulates a camera rack focus combined with zoom. Start with the text slightly blurred (blur 2px) and at 98% scale, then animate to sharp focus (blur 0px) and 100% scale over the first second. After the focus pull, begin the continuous slow zoom from 100% to 102%. This creates a cinematic entrance that draws attention before settling into the meditative zoom. The blur-to-focus transition should use an ease-out curve to mimic real camera focus behavior. Consider adding a subtle brightness adjustment during the focus pull to simulate depth of field changes.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Use BaseLayout with 'relative w-full h-full overflow-hidden'. Apply a TextAtom with multiple synchronized effects. Create a blur effect: [{at: 0, value: 2}, {at: 0.1, value: 0}] with easing: 'ease-out'. Scale effect with two phases: [{at: 0, value: 0.98}, {at: 0.1, value: 1}, {at: 1, value: 1.02}]. Add brightness effect: [{at: 0, value: 0.9}, {at: 0.1, value: 1}]. Use 'transition-all duration-1000' for the initial focus pull if using CSS transitions, or rely on the effects system. Typography: 'text-6xl font-light text-center'. The filter property can combine blur and brightness: `blur(${blur}px) brightness(${brightness})`. Consider adding will-change: 'filter, transform' for optimization.

prompts.prompt: Create a quantum zoom preset where the text appears to exist in multiple scale states simultaneously before collapsing into the slow zoom. Use CSS blend modes and multiple copies of the text at different scales (98%, 100%, 102%) with low opacity (20-30%). Over the first 1-2 seconds, fade out the alternate scales while fading in the main text, creating a quantum collapse effect. Then begin the standard slow zoom. This creates an ethereal, dreamlike quality that suggests multiple possibilities before settling into reality. Think of it as showing the 'probability cloud' of where the text might be before it materializes.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Create multiple BaseLayout containers with 'absolute inset-0 flex items-center justify-center'. Generate 3-4 copies of the TextAtom, each with different initial scales (0.98, 1.0, 1.02, 1.04) and opacity: 0.3. Use mix-blend-mode: 'screen' or 'overlay' for ethereal overlapping. Apply opacity effects to fade out alternate copies: [{at: 0, value: 0.3}, {at: 0.15, value: 0}] while main copy fades in: [{at: 0, value: 0.3}, {at: 0.15, value: 1}]. After collapse, apply continuous scale to main: [{at: 0.15, value: 1}, {at: 1, value: 1.02}]. Use 'pointer-events-none' on ghost copies. Consider using a sub-preset for the quantum collapse effect that can be reused.

prompts.prompt: Design a lens distortion zoom preset that simulates the subtle barrel distortion of a real camera lens during zoom. Instead of uniform scaling, create a slight fishbowl effect that's stronger at the edges. The center zooms normally (100% to 102%) while the edges zoom slightly more (100% to 103%), creating a subtle warping effect. Use CSS transforms with a custom transform matrix or combine scale with a subtle perspective distortion. This mimics the optical characteristics of real camera lenses, adding a photographic quality to the typography animation.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Use BaseLayout with 'relative w-full h-full overflow-hidden'. Apply a perspective container with style={{ perspective: '2000px' }}. For the distortion effect, split text into multiple spans or use SVG filters if available. Create a custom transform that combines scale with rotateX and rotateY based on position from center. Center text scales normally: [{at: 0, value: 1}, {at: 1, value: 1.02}]. Edge characters get additional transforms. Alternatively, use CSS filter with a custom SVG filter for barrel distortion. Typography: 'text-7xl font-thin'. Consider using transform: `scale(${scale}) rotate3d(0.1, 0.1, 0, ${rotation}deg)` for pseudo-distortion. Add 'transform-gpu antialiased' for smooth rendering.

prompts.prompt: Build a heartbeat zoom preset where the continuous zoom has a subtle rhythmic pulse overlaid, like a heartbeat or breathing rhythm. The base zoom goes from 100% to 102%, but every 1.5 seconds, add a tiny 'bump' that temporarily increases the scale by 0.2% over 200ms before returning. This creates a living, organic quality. Sync these pulses with audio beats if available, or use a fixed rhythm for a meditative effect. The pulses should be felt more than seen - like feeling the cameraman's heartbeat through a handheld shot.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Create BaseLayout with 'flex items-center justify-center w-full h-full'. In presetExecution, calculate pulse points every 1.5 seconds (or sync with audio beats if available via fetcher). Build an AnimationRange array that includes the base linear progression plus small bumps: generate keyframes like [{at: 0, value: 1}, {at: 0.15, value: 1.002}, {at: 0.151, value: 1.0022}, {at: 0.155, value: 1.002}, ...]. Use cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.6, 1) for pulse easing. If audio data is available, use waveform effects with 'zoom' type and low sensitivity (0.1-0.2) to create audio-reactive pulses. Typography: 'text-5xl font-light tracking-wide'. Consider using internal effect presets if 'heartbeat' or 'pulse' effects exist.

prompts.prompt: Create a microscopic zoom preset that simulates looking at text through a microscope slowly increasing magnification. Start with a subtle chromatic aberration effect (RGB channels slightly offset) that decreases as the zoom increases, mimicking optical correction at higher magnification. The zoom should feel scientific and precise, going from 100% to 102.5% with perfect linear motion. Add a subtle vignette effect that increases slightly during zoom, and consider adding grain or noise texture that becomes more visible as we 'zoom in closer' to the text surface.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Use BaseLayout with 'relative w-full h-full bg-gray-50'. Create three TextAtom copies for RGB channels, each with 'absolute inset-0 mix-blend-screen'. Apply different colors via filter or text color: red channel with 'text-red-500', green normal, blue with 'text-blue-500'. Offset red by translateX: -1px initially, blue by translateX: 1px. During zoom, reduce offsets to 0. Main scale effect: [{at: 0, value: 1}, {at: 1, value: 1.025}] with linear easing. Add vignette using radial-gradient background or pseudo-element with 'absolute inset-0 pointer-events-none' and radial gradient opacity. For grain, add noise texture via CSS filter or background-image. Consider using filter: 'contrast(1.1) saturate(0.9)' for scientific look. Typography: 'font-mono text-6xl'. The chromatic aberration creates a unique visual signature.
